title: A complete authorisation-code + PKCE round-trip issues a project session
asA: operator signing in through the project's OAuth2 sign-in surface
iWant: the browser to be redirected to the provider's authorise endpoint, to be redirected back with a code, and to end up holding a project session cookie
soThat: the project treats me as authenticated on subsequent requests without re-presenting credentials to the provider

acceptanceCriteria.description: The initial GET on the project's sign-in route redirects to the provider's authorise endpoint with `response_type=code`, a non-empty `code_challenge`, `code_challenge_method=S256`, and a `state` value not present in any prior redirect within the test's observation window.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a project wired to a mock OIDC provider through the provider-config module and a browser that hits GET `/auth/sign-in?provider=<id>`
acceptanceCriteria.when: the request is dispatched and the response is inspected
acceptanceCriteria.then: the response is a 302 to the provider's declared `authorizeUrl`; the location query carries `response_type=code`, `code_challenge` (matches `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{43,128}$`), `code_challenge_method=S256`, a `state` value distinct from any previously observed value in the test's collector; no `access_type=implicit` or `response_type=token` is present

acceptanceCriteria.description: The callback with a valid code and matching state redeems the code at the provider's token endpoint using the PKCE verifier and receives an access token plus (for OIDC) an id_token.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the mock provider has minted an authorisation code for the pending flow keyed by the state value from AC-10101-1
acceptanceCriteria.when: the browser follows the provider's redirect back to the project's callback route
acceptanceCriteria.then: the flow controller issues a POST to the provider's `tokenUrl` whose body carries `grant_type=authorization_code`, the returned `code`, `client_id`, `code_verifier` (matching the pending-flow record), and `redirect_uri`; the response is a 2xx with `access_token`; for an OIDC provider the response additionally carries an `id_token`

acceptanceCriteria.description: The callback completes with a Secure HttpOnly session cookie whose value is a project-issued opaque handle, not a provider token.
acceptanceCriteria.when: the browser inspects the response cookie jar
acceptanceCriteria.then: a session cookie declared by the project's session-cookie name (per config) is set with `Secure`, `HttpOnly`, and `SameSite=Lax`; the cookie value does not equal the access token, the id_token, or any refresh token returned by the provider; the value matches the opaque-handle shape declared by the session-bridge
